description: Rules that report on a dotted member and go SILENT when the same member is written o['k'] — the notation bundlers and minifiers emit. SHRINK-ONLY: a rule may leave this list, never join it. Produced by scripts/find-computed-key-blind-spots.mts.
why: Rules that report on one spelling of a property and go silent on another. The probe rewrites three shapes now: a CALL (obj.m() -> obj['m']()), a READ (obj.p -> obj['p']), and an object literal KEY ({ k: v } -> { ['k']: v }). Calls alone reached 282 of 470 rules and found 0 blind; adding reads reached 349 and found 22, all since fixed; adding KEYS reached 3,130 cases and found 50 more. The key class is the largest because `check:spellings` counts 195 bare-object-key sites against 117 dotted ones, and until now none of the 195 was exercised by any direct instrument. Every entry here is a rule whose own true positive stops reporting when its config object is written the way a minifier writes it — cors({ ['origin']: '*' }), { ['rejectUnauthorized']: false }, jwt.sign({ ['password']: '...' }). Shrink-only: a rule may leave this list, never join it. On 2026-11-07 the probe began replaying each case through the harness its test file wraps around it (docs/intents/the-ledger-records-fragments-not-files): evidence-gated rules had been probed on bare fragments that never fired, so 1,645 TP cases in 121 rules were silently outside the instrument. Reaching them raised the probed count from 4,466 to 6,960 and found 38 more rules that go silent on a string subscript — e.g. express-security/no-permissive-cors on app['use'](cors({ ['origin']: '*' })). They are recorded here as found debt, the same way the read and key extensions were; the list stays shrink-only.

known_probe_artefacts.nestjs-security/no-permissive-cors: A TYPE position: `const c: common.CorsOptions`. `common['CorsOptions']` is a valid indexed-access type, so it parses, but types are ERASED before a bundler emits anything — a subscripted type annotation cannot occur in the code this probe exists to model. Left listed rather than special-cased in the rewrite, so the judgement stays visible and reviewable.
known_probe_artefacts.browser-security/no-insecure-redirects: Removed 2026-09-02: it was never blind. The read rewrite had reached inside a REGEX literal, turning /^https:\/\/a\.example\.com/ into a["example"]. Regex literals now pass through untouched.
known_probe_artefacts.(spelling-contrast cases): Three rules left this list without a code change: react-class-to-hooks and no-direct-mutation-state were FIXED, while no-improper-type-validation was never blind — its case deliberately mixes `bag["k"]` with `bag.k`, and the rewrite normalised both, matching a guard the case exists to keep unmatched. The probe now skips a case containing both spellings of the same member.
